Matthew has journaled most of his life. In prepping to write this book, he took his life's journals and isolated himself to read through the journals and recall key moments from his life: experiences, lessons learned (and re-learned), beliefs, approaches to life, and catching what he has termed "greenlights". Seizing opportunities life presents you and how to recognize them. He also shares how road blocks- or as he calls them, "red lights"- sometimes become greenlights later on in life.

This book encourages self-reflection and personal growth. It shares the importance of connecting with yourself and pushing yourself outside your comfort zone to truly get to know the true you! It's a celebration of life and the journey of living.
Quick read.

STORY
From Matthew himself: “An album, a record, a story of my life so far. This is fifty years of my sights and seens, felts and figured-outs, cools and shamefuls. Graces, truths, and beauties of brutality. Getting away withs, getting caughts, and getting wets while trying to dance between the raindrops.”

STARS
Listening to Matthew McConaughey narrate his own “love letter to life” as he calls it was pure joy. His accent and enthusiasm made this such an engaging story to partake in.

I laughed, I cried, and I gained wisdom from the many stories portrayed in this memoir. I mostly enjoyed the ending where he talked about his beautiful wife and family.

Green Light!

SPICE
While there aren’t any explicitly sexy scenes, Matthew doesn’t shy away from talking about sex. His own father died whilst in the middle of an intimate moment with his wife… and Matthew doesn’t shy away from talking about ANY of it.

HAPPY ENDING
Matthew McConaughey lives a beautiful life. His story isn’t over, but his memoir ended on a lovely note.

FINAL THOUGHTS
How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days is my favorite romantic comedy movie! As a Matthew fan, I am glad that I listened to his memoir and would 100% recommend the audio version of Green Lights.

Admittedly, I started reading McConaughey's memoir with preconceived notions. He was the golden boy of the early 2000s rom-coms, an undeniable Hollywood charm machine. But "Greenlights" shattered that carefully crafted image, revealing a more accurate depiction of the man beneath the Texas drawl.

The raw honesty about his upbringing was eye-opening. His parents’ toxic divorce cycle, the physical and emotional abuse, the teenage rebellion – these weren't Hollywood anecdotes, they were formative experiences that shaped him. It humanized him, allowing us to understand how his past informed his present, how resilience bloomed from broken pieces.

But "Greenlights" isn't a sob story. He doesn't paint himself as a victim; instead, he walks through life with a contagious "just keep livin'" attitude. He acknowledges his privilege, the childhood treehouses and early confidence-building opportunities available to him, but doesn't shy away from highlighting the inequalities that others face. His storm-into-the-producer's-office anecdote is a stark reminder of the different doors that swing open for certain demographics.

McConaughey's positive outlook isn't blind positivity. It's a conscious choice, nurtured by introspection and self-awareness. He encourages going back to your roots, reflecting on your journey, and taking charge of your narrative. His mantra, "sometimes which choice you make is not as important as making a choice and committing to it," resonated deeply, offering a new perspective on making decisions in an uncertain world.

Matthew McConaughey makes a great case for getting off the daily treadmill grind to take time for personal reflection and centering. This book is his journey to find his core values - and it’s a refreshing take on things. His anecdotes are raw, honest, without borders. His words are crafted for self-discovery, not to fit an image. His audio book delivery hits hard in the beginning pages, almost like a revival sermon. And it’s a jarring delivery, so much so that I almost stopped reading. However, I slowed the audio speed a bit and gave the narrative time to melt. It soon hits a rewarding rhythm. This book is all about finding life’s balance.

It’s hard to believe that all the stories in this book are true. A 13-story tree house? McConaughey mentions at one point that his older brother is a millionaire, but his parents are struggling. His mother broke his father’s nose and then they made love on the kitchen floor? (Where were the kids?) These sound like tall tales. His parents seem questionable in their parenting skills. If my mother threw me in a river and told me to swim or drown, I would’ve drowned. McConaughey is a unique person and I admire that he doesn’t seem materialistic and is introspective. His choice of movie roles is interesting and he’s a gifted actor. This memoir is definitely different and has some good advice. It’s upbeat and optimistic which is why I chose to read it. If this book is based on 35 years of his journals, I’m sure it could’ve easily been 1,000 pages, so I appreciate that it’s not. However, I had trouble reading some of the inserted text on my Kindle. This should’ve been formatted better, or he could’ve left some of it out and added another story or two from his life.

I listened to the audio version of GREENLIGHTS written and narrated by Matthew McConaughey.

MY RATING GUIDE: 4 Satisfied Stars. I found GREENLIGHTS a thought provoking listen.
1= dnf/What was that?; 2= Nope, not for me; 3= This was okay/cute; 3.5= I enjoyed it; 4= A WORTHWHILE READ; 5= I Loved it, it was great! (I seldom give 5 Stars).

What I Liked ~
1) GREENLIGHTS is a candid audio biography of McConaughey’s life and lessons he has learned thus far. I found it honest, whether or not I agreed with his choices.
2) I found GREENLIGHTS thought provoking. I was challenged to consider my own life, how I am living it, what changes I might make in whatever time I have left.
3) GREENLIGHTS contains a lot of content, so much that I doubt I will remember all the challenges from one listen. That being the case, I imagine I will obtain a copy and listen again at some point in the future.
4) I don’t generally read/enjoy memoirs, biographies or audio biographies, since people are simply people and I don’t believe in idolizing particular ones. I do appreciate history and lessons learned from it, however, and I enjoy asking questions. McConaughey presents questions. Answers are found when we Unplug and search for them ourselves.
5) McConaughey‘s narrative of his own thoughts presents GREENLIGHTS as real and sincere.

My Takeaway ~
As people and individuals we need to Unplug, at least occasionally, to reconsider who we are, where we are heading, who are we following, and then make the necessary changes to return to what is true.

Recommended to readers who~
1) Enjoy asking questions and/or those who seek to better themselves and the world we live in, beginning with self-introspection and personal reflection.
2) Wonder about Matthew McConaughey’s nature, attitudes, character, values - as an actor and the individual.

READER CAUTION ~
PROFANITY - Yes. Strong language is used.
SEXUAL SITUATIONS - None. No details.
VIOLENCE - G.

A raw honest self examination and reflection of his background and beliefs. Not my favorite book, but it is obvious why it is popular. Despite espousing to thine own self be true...it ends with bowing to a populist world view. Highly recommended to me, I can't do the same. I enjoyed reading it, and I liked getting to know more about Matthew... Maybe even admiring him. He is a good writer, and a pretty fair story teller. We already knew he's a remarkable actor. It was worth my time reading it.

An inspiring listen that is surprisingly (and mostly refreshingly) honest. There are a few parts that might not be suitable to all ears (perhaps), but I really enjoyed it. Not too long. Gets right into it. I'd say more but I'm skipping the 'koolaid' part of a review.

It was a good book, told by the author. The thing s he has done in his life and the way he expresses his values make me impresses with him as a artist and actor. I would recommend this book if you like him as a person or not.
Enlightening and entertaining. Reads like McConaughey talks which is very philosophical and sometimes wordy, but I appreciated the character it gave to the stories.

I listened to this book on Audible as I drove to work every day until I finished it. I live in Waikoloa and work in Kona so about a 40 minute drive. I found it very amusing and fun to listen to. Matthew read the book and he had such enthusiasm doing it. What an interesting life this man has led and continues to live. I have liked him as an actor in his rom com roles, even though he wants more challenging characters to portray. I admire that the most important thing to him is being a dad to his 3 children.
This started slowly but just like fine wine,kept getting better all the way through. Recommend it for all who enjoy real life stories

Sincere, honest, flamboyant describe this McConaughey autobiography. A blazingl review of his life and his thoughtful analysis of what kind of life fits him and how to live it according to his values.

This book was pretty good, when read by the author. I can see how it would seem rambling and incoherent if you were just reading it. His voice and inflection brings life to the stories he tells. He has lived an interesting life and has an interesting perspective.

Lo más importante del relato es cómo se manifiestan los valores familiares de Matthew a lo largo de su vida. Cómo las raíces familiares lo guiaron a tomar desiciones siempre basándose en sus creencias.

I learned that I did not know Matthew McConaughey Like I thought I kinda might just from the roles he has played. Duh! He is acting.

I don’t agree with everything he thinks is a great lesson and/But that doesn’t mean he isn’t a superb actor and a well written author.

I didn’t like the suck it up buttercup way of learning lessons ……..I found his upbringing full of trauma. It broke my heart that he seemed to find a lot of it normal.

I love how eccentric he is. I love unique people. I love how he loves his wife and kids. And family.

It was a good read. His notes were a bit distracting.

Very unique read.
This was a fun "listen" kind of book. I would not have enjoyed it nearly as much without the author narrating.

I'm not a big memoir reader, but I liked this one a lot. I listened on audio. And it was so good! From a rough and dysfunctional upbringing to talent and luck, McConaughey takes on us on a delightful ride full of greenlights (and some red ones, too)!
